android_mechanism: Unchanged items re-processed (rehashed) on every refresh; fix skips unchanged items cheaply
bug_description: insertArticle detects duplicates by letting the UNIQUE(feed_id, guid) constraint fail and catching the thrown exception ('Duplicate entry, ignore'). Every feed refresh re-attempts inserts for ALL previously seen articles — each one a full insert attempt that ends in a constraint-violation exception (statement execution + error object construction + catch), multiplying refresh cost with stored article count.
fix_summary: Inserts run with ConflictResolution.ON_CONFLICT_IGNORE so SQLite silently skips duplicates without exception overhead; behavior (only new articles stored) is unchanged.
trigger_steps: Subscribe to feeds with substantial history and refresh once to populate articles.
Start hitrace capture (categories: app, sched, disk, database).
Trigger refresh-all again (all articles already exist; every insert is a duplicate).
Stop hitrace when refresh completes. Repeat 3 repetitions for unfixed, then install the fixed HAP and repeat 3 repetitions.

test_oracle.definition: CPU time across the no-op refresh case window, from trace.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed pays statement-execution + exception-throw/catch per stored article; fixed pays a cheap ignored insert. unfixed no-op refresh CPU > fixed by a clear margin scaling with stored article count.

oracle_revision.previous_definition: CPU time of the refresh phase when nothing new arrives (all duplicate inserts), from trace + JS sampling (exception handling frames).
oracle_revision.corrected_definition: CPU time across the no-op refresh case window, from trace.
oracle_revision.reason: WEAKER PROXY. The declared metric names CPU for the no-op refresh phase, and trace_cpu_ms is collected - but on this case the two variants OVERLAP: 23463.5/27458.4/37015.4 unfixed vs 24176.7/25597.2/26290.9 fixed, a 13.5% reduction with the ranges interleaved. So the declared metric is collected and does not separate the variants; the main-thread CPU field does (no overlap, 16.4%). This is the honest reading rather than a pass: the case does not reach a clear difference on the metric it declares. An earlier revision claimed the rounds collected only elapsed_ms, which was wrong.

trace_config.command: hdc shell hitrace --time 60 app sched disk database -o /data/local/tmp/sr_dupinsert.chtrace
